title: Collector identity envelope and edge trace convergence
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: For dedicated and on-prem deployments we often receive heterogeneous telemetry from edge proxies, SDKs, and partner relays. This ticket implements a lightweight per-collector identity envelope and a deterministic trace-context canonicalization layer so traces and logs stitched at the platform are reliably attributed and deduplicated across replay/forwarding scenarios. Goals: 1) Provide a compact collector identity envelope that rides alongside OTLP/JSON payloads without breaking existing pipelines; 2) Normalize trace context fields (traceparent, tracestate variants, tenant tags) to a single canonical form at ingest; 3) Produce a replay-safe provenance header that allows safe re-ingest and deduplication in the presence of buffering and retries; 4) Add dashboards that surface convergence issues (mismatched ids, uncertain parentage) and SLIs for attach-rate and dedupe effectiveness.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Collector identity envelope spec published and reviewed by security and infra; 2) Ingest path accepts and validates the envelope without dropping existing telemetry; 3) Trace-context canonicalizer reduces mismatched-parent traces by >= 90% in synthetic test traffic; 4) Replay-safe provenance header present on replays and used by dedupe stage; 5) Grafana dashboard surfaces attach-rate, canonicalization failures, and dedupe ratios; 6) Feature gated behind runtime flag and rollout plan completed to 3 pilot Dedicated customers with no data loss incidents.
design_notes: High-level design: - Envelope: minimal header with collector_id (UUID v4), clock_offset_ms, version, and a compact signature token (HMAC-SHA256) computed with per-tenant signing key in KMS; header serialized as base64 JSON to avoid protocol changes. - Canonicalizer: set of ordered rules that map incoming trace fields to the canonical tuple (trace_id, span_id, parent_id, tenant_id, sampled). Rules include: prefer W3C traceparent, fall back to X-Cloud-Trace or legacy headers, normalize tracestate ordering, collapse tenant tags from headers/body into standardized tenant_id. - Dedupe / replay-safety: provenance header contains origin collector_id and monotonic sequence window; ingestion maintains short-lived watermark table (TTL 5m) to detect duplicates from buffered replays. - Security: signature verification required for Private deployments; for Hosted we accept unsigned envelopes but mark provenance as unverified. Trade-offs: HMAC adds CPU at ingress; we mitigate by validating only when header present and batching signature checks. We considered full PKI but chose HMAC for lower operational burden and KMS integration.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): feature flag off by default, deploy canonicalizer + envelope parser to ingest nodes in staging; run in observation-only mode for 2 weeks. Phase 2 (pilot): enable signed-envelope validation for 3 pilot Dedicated tenants with sidecar upgrades; collect metrics and run synthetic replay tests. Phase 3 (gradual): enable dedupe and provenance enforcement across Dedicated and Private clusters with 10% traffic ramps every 48 hours. Phase 4 (opt-in for Hosted): roll out unsigned-envelope parsing and attach provenance metadata but keep policy lax. Rollback: feature flag disable restores previous behavior instantly; we maintain compatibility shim for collectors that do not emit header.
test_plan: Unit tests for canonicalizer mapping rules and signature verification. Integration tests: synthetic generator that emits mixed header formats and simulated buffering/replay; assert dedupe effectiveness and correct canonicalization. Performance tests: sig-verify microbench to ensure <1ms median per-check under single-threaded workload; end-to-end ingest throughput regression test to confirm <5% latency p95 regression when parser enabled. Staging load test against existing private cluster with 10k rps for 1 hour. Acceptance runbook includes step-by-step checks for attach-rate and SLI thresholds.
